newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics shares hot on modem speculation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics shares hot on modem speculation.

text.p: Shares of U.S. Robotics Corp soared 9-1/2 on Tuesday to 78-5/8 after the company said it would introduce a new technology on Wednesday that some analysts believe might be a long-awaited faster modem.

The stock has risen in past weeks as well amid speculation it would launch a modem for telecommunication connection at speeds of 56 kilobits per second. The fastest modem currently on the market is 33.6 kbps.
"That's my expectation," said Rakesh Sood, an analyst for Hambrecht & Quist.
The company said in a statement it would "unveil one of the most exciting new technologies ever to be developed by U.S. Robotics." It said it would also announce broad-based strategic alliances.
"It's really, really big," a U.S. Robotics spokeswoman said. She said she could not provide additional information on the announcement.
Other companies have already said they would unveil the 56-kbps technology. U.S. Robotics has maintained it does not think the 33.6 kbps modem currently in the market is the fastest possible.
Analysts said they expect U.S. Robotics to unveil the modem, the online service hub to which users connect, as well as alliances with companies who will use the company's products.
Amar Senan, an analyst for Volpe, Welty & Co, said alliances with Internet service providers who will use the 56 kbps products are something other modem makers have yet to announce.
U.S. Robotics clients currently include America Online Inc, Compuserve Corp, AT&T WorldNet and Netcom On-Line Communications Inc, Senan said.
"It's going to say 'We've got the hubs, the modems, plus the customers'," Senan said. "In that way they will upstage all the other companies who have made announcements."
Motorola Inc, for example, said it would unveil a 56 kbps modem in 1997, and Rockwell International Corp said it expects to demonstrate the technology at a trade show in November.
The analysts said, however, they do not expect the 56-kbps modem to be available until early 1997.
"It has been expected for some time. The question is the availability," Sood said. "I'm a little surprised the stock moved so much."
Senan said the industry would likely need time to develop a standard. U.S. Robotics, for example, will need to see what Rockwell is planning, he said.
"It is in everyone's interest to make sure the technologies are compatible," Senan said.
